title: I Am the Way, the Truth, and the Life

verses.text: Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe in Me as well.
In My Father's house are many rooms; if it were not so, I would have told you. I am going there to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.
You know the way to the place where I am going."
"Lord," said Thomas, "we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?"
Jesus answered, "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
If you had known Me, you would know My Father as well. From now on you do know Him and have seen Him."
Philip said, "Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us."
Jesus replied, "Have I been among you all this time, and you still do not know Me, Philip? Whoever has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, 'Show us the Father'?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me? The words I speak to you I do not speak on My own authority. It is the Father, dwelling in Me, who does His work.
Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me, or at least believe on account of the works themselves.
Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in Me will also do the works I have been doing, and he will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
You may ask Me for anything in My name, and I will do it.
If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Helper to be with you forever—
the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you know Him, for He dwells with you and will be in you.
I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.
On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.
Whoever has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. And whoever loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and disclose Myself to him."
Judas (not Iscariot) asked Him, "Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered, "If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word. My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
Whoever does not love Me does not keep My words. And the word you hear is not My own, but the Father's who sent Me.
All these things I have spoken to you while I am still with you.
But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and remind you of everything I have told you.
Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled or afraid.
You heard Me tell you, 'I am going away, and I am coming back to you.' If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I.
I have told you this now before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.
I will not speak with you much longer, for the ruler of this world is coming. He has no claim on Me,
but he comes so that the world may know that I love the Father and do exactly as the Father has commanded Me. Rise, let us go from here.

context.author: Traditionally the apostle John
context.genre: Theological narrative — Jesus' extended private comfort and instruction to His disciples, continuing the same night as chapter 13
context.audience: A broad, likely mixed Jewish and Gentile readership toward the end of the first century
context.setting: Still the same evening as the foot washing, in the upper room — a moment of quiet instruction sandwiched between Judas's departure into the night and Jesus' prayer and arrest still to come.
context.custom: A first-century household's father commonly added rooms onto the family home as sons married and stayed within it — a familiar, homely picture behind Jesus' promise of "many rooms" prepared for His disciples in His Father's house, rather than a picture of a distant hotel.
context.timelineImmediate: This chapter continues the same unbroken night conversation begun in chapter 13, moving from comfort about His departure, through three individual disciples' questions (Thomas, Philip, Judas not Iscariot), to Jesus' promise of the Holy Spirit and His parting gift of peace — closing with the words "rise, let us go," though the discourse itself actually continues for three more chapters before they leave the room.
context.timelineBible: Jesus' promise of "another Helper" uses a Greek word (paraklētos) meaning one called alongside to help or advocate — the same term used for Jesus Himself in 1 John 2:1, suggesting the Spirit's coming role continues rather than replaces His own.
context.sparkNotes: Jesus comforts His troubled disciples with the promise of many rooms prepared for them in His Father's house, and answers Thomas's confused question about the way there with one of His boldest claims: "I am the way and the truth and the life." Philip's request to simply see the Father draws out Jesus' direct claim that to see Him is to see the Father Himself. The chapter closes with the promise of the Holy Spirit as a permanent Helper and Jesus' gift of a peace unlike anything the world can offer.

translation.english: I am the way, the truth, and the life
translation.greek: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωή (egō eimi hē hodos kai hē alētheia kai hē zōē)
translation.meaning: The sixth of Jesus' seven great "I am" declarations in John — not simply claiming to show a way, but to personally be the only path to the Father, an exclusive claim that has shaped Christian theology ever since.

Literally "one called alongside" — an advocate, comforter, or counselor summoned to help in a time of need. This same Greek word is used of Jesus Himself in 1 John 2:1, suggesting real continuity between Christ's own ministry and the Spirit's.

Echoes the Hebrew shalom, a rich word for wholeness and well-being far beyond the absence of conflict — Jesus explicitly distinguishes His gift from the world's fragile, circumstance-dependent version of peace.

otBackground.note: Moses' request to see God's glory, met with the reply that no one can see God's face and live — background for the weight of Philip's request and Jesus' remarkable answer.
The priestly blessing of peace — background for the richer, more personal peace Jesus promises to leave with His disciples.
God's Spirit guiding and comforting His people in the wilderness — an early picture of the Helper's promised comforting role.

mapCoords.placeName: The Upper Room, Mount Zion, Jerusalem

commentary.note: Henry traces the Greek word behind 'mansions' (monai) to a root meaning 'abiding places' — not temporary lodging but durable dwelling: 'here we are as in an inn; in heaven we shall gain a settlement.' He notes the disciples had given up their own houses to follow Christ, 'who had not where to lay his head, but the mansions in heaven will make them amends.'

Wesley sees Jesus answering three separate questions in one sentence. Thomas had asked about the way, so Jesus says "I am the way"; the question of knowing, so "I am the truth"; the question of where He was going, so "I am the life." He adds that verse 4's "way" is "of faith, holiness, sufferings," and that verse 26 is a clear promise to the apostles that the Spirit would teach them all the truth needed for salvation.

This Victorian collection of sermon outlines stresses that the Greek behind "mansions" (monai) means abiding dwelling-places, and that Jesus is describing a Father's house, not a hotel: "no wayside inn, no temporary abode." It adds that heaven is therefore "no unknown land, no land of strangers" for believers, but a home prepared for a family that will always live there.

overview.summary: Jesus tells the troubled disciples that He is going to prepare a place for them, and that He is the way, the truth, and the life. He promises the Holy Spirit as the Helper and leaves His peace with them.

history.t: The Father's house pictures a large home with space for the family.
Philip wanted to see the Father, and Jesus said seeing Him is seeing the Father.

customs.t: A groom prepared a room at his father's house before the wedding.
Peace was the usual Jewish greeting, meaning wholeness, not only calm.

archaeology.t: The Crusader-era building on Mount Zion marks the traditional upper room.
Houses in Jerusalem's upper city had multiple rooms around a courtyard.

overview.discussion: Jesus said, "Let not your hearts be troubled." What troubles you most tonight?
